 JUDGMENT
Plaintiff instituted this suit against the defendant for partition and permanent injunction.
2. The case of the plaintiff is that she is the daughter of defendant No.1.
The defendant No.1 is the wife of late Nanjunda Reddy, who is the son of late Motamma wife of late Muninanjappa.
Late Motamma and late Muninanjappa got 5 children.
Out of them late Nanjunda Reddy was their third son.

The plaintiff's grandmother late Smt.Motamma was the absolute owner of property bearing Sy.No.191/1 of Agara village, Begur Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk, which was acquired by the BDA for formation of HSR Layout.
The said property had fallen to the share of plaintiff's father as there was oral partition between the children of late Motamma.
After the death of plaintiff's father, the mother of the plaintiff i.e defendant No.1 was looking after the properties which fell to the share of late Nanjundappa.
The said property was acquired by BDA measuring east-west 12.19 meters and north- south 18.90 meters, totally 230.39 square meters under incentive scheme.
Thereafter on 5/11/2001, the BDA has executed a sale deed in favour of defendant No.1.
After marriage of plaintiff to Sri.Krishna Reddy, she had been residing with her husband in Andhra Pradesh.
Due to some problem the plaintiff came back to Bengaluru and asked her mother defendant No.1 for partition.
The defendant No.1 initially agreed but later refused.
The plaintiff is not interested to continue in the joint family and she had been continuously demanding for partition and defendant No.1 went on postponing the same on one pretext or the other.
The suit schedule property is the ancestral property and plaintiff has got legitimate share in the same.
Except plaintiff and defendant No.1 no one else has any semblance of right, interest or title in any manner over the suit schedule property.
The defendant No.1 without the knowledge of plaintiff has sold away the suit schedule property to defendant No.2.

On account of the said fact the plaintiff has caused legal injury to the extent of her Prameela N vs Lakshmamma on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92622320/
2 half share in the suit schedule property and the said alienation is not binding on the plaintiff and now the defendant No.2 is trying to alienate the schedule property with the sole intention to deprive the plaintiff's right.
Hence this suit.
3. Upon issuance of suit summons, defendants No.1 to 3 appeared before the court through their counsels and filed written statement separately.
4. The defendant No.1 in her written statement admitted the contention of the plaintiff and prayed to allow the suit.

5.Defendant No.2 filed his written statement by denying the averments made in the plaint in para wise and contended that the plaintiff is a stranger to the family of Smt.Lakshmamma and Nanjunda Reddy and there was no property bearing Sy.No.119/1 in Agara village and therefore the whole claim of the plaintiff is false and the question of claiming partition will not arise.
The false averment made by the plaintiff that the property belonged to late Nanjunda Reddy.

Smt.Lakshmamma approached the BDA and sought for allotment under the scheme called Voluntary Surrender Scheme and the application of Smt.Lakshmamma was considered and allotment is made purely in favour of Smt.Lakshmamma and therefore the property becomes separate property of Smt.Lakshmamma.

The property acquired in the year 1987 and allotment was made in the year 2000 and therefore the amended provision of Section 6 of Hindu Succession Act is not applicable to the facts and circumstances of the case.
Therefore the plaintiff cannot claim any share in respect of the property which is allotted by the BDA in favour of Smt.Lakshmamma.
The allotment was made for a valuable consideration and a consideration of Rs.17,800/- was paid by Smt.Lakshmamma.
On payment of the said amount the said property was conveyed in favour of Smt.Lakshmamma and hence the said property is the absolute and separate property of Smt.Lakshmamma.
Plaintiff did not lay her claim for grant of compensation for receiving the compensation of Rs.3,40,847/-.
The plaintiff really having a share in the property, the remedy available is to seek for a share in the compensation amount of Rs.3,40,847/- which was deposited by the BDA.
Therefore the claim of plaintiff with respect to schedule property is frivolous and mischievous.
The plaintiff did not seek for any share in the property, the acquisition of which was complete during the year 1987.
For the first time the plaintiff is seeking the claim in the year 2011 which is after a period of 12 years.
Therefore the plaintiff is not entitled to any relief since her claim is barred by time under law.

The plaintiff made false averment that the property was allotted to the share of Nanjunda Reddy under family partition,
but the plaintiff failed to aver the date of such partition and failed to produce the partition deed to show that the said property was allotted to the share of Nanjunda Reddy.
The mutation was also never made out in favour of either Nanjunda Reddy or Lakshmamma, which shows that the claim of the plaintiff is false.
The property which was acquired by the government for the benefit of BDA was the property bearing Sy.No.119/1 measuring 4 acres 10 guntas.
The said property belonged to one Motamma.
At no point of time there was any partition between Motamma and her children and the said property was the absolute property of Motamma.
After completion of acquisition proceedings a compensation of Rs.3,40,847/- was deposited in the civil court since all the legal heirs of Motamma had right over the said compensation.

The defendant No.2 is not aware as to the allocation of the compensation amount by the court and however on verification, since Smt.Lakshmamma was a member of the family of Motamma, she approached for allotment of a site.

The application Prameela N vs Lakshmamma on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92622320/
3 preferred by Lakshmamma in her individual capacity was considered and the allotment was made exclusively to Smt.Lakshmamma and not for the benefit of the family.

sentences.text: Moreover there was no joint family concept existing in view of the absence of even a single male member of the family.
Therefore it is a fallacy to claim that schedule properties are ancestral property.
Hence defendant No.2 prayed to dismiss the suit with costs.

3. Whether there is cause of action?
4. Whether suit is barred by limitation?
5. Whether the court fee paid is insufficient?
6. Whether plaintiff is entitle for the partition and separate possession?

If so, what is her share?
7.
Whether the plaintiff is entitled for reliefs sought for?
8. What order or decree?

ADDITIONAL ISSUE:
1.

Whether suit of the plaintiff barred under Section 14 of Hindu Succession Act,
1956?

sentences.text: On the other hand the defendant No.2 is examined as DW1 and re-iterated the written statement averments in his affidavit filed in lieu of examination-in-chief.

As per the version of D.W.1 stated that he obtained the suit schedule property by way of registered sale deed executed by mother of plaintiff i.e. defendant No.1 and he is in possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property.

Defendant No.1 approached the BDA and sought for allotment under the scheme called Voluntary Surrender Scheme and the application of defendant No.1 was considered and allotment is made purely in favour of defendant No.1 and therefore the property becomes separate property of defendant No.1.

The property acquired in the year 1987 and allotment was made in the year 2000 and therefore the amended provision of Section 6 of Hindu Succession Act is not applicable to the facts and circumstances of the case.
Therefore the plaintiff cannot claim any share in respect of the property which is allotted by the BDA in favour of defendant No.1.
The allotment was made for a valuable consideration and a consideration of Rs.17,800/- was paid by defendant No.1.
On payment of the said amount the said property was conveyed in favour of defendant No.1 and hence the said property is the absolute and separate property of defendant No.1.
Therefore the claim of plaintiff with respect to schedule property is frivolous and mischievous.
The plaintiff did not seek for any share in the property, the acquisition of which was complete during the year 1987.
For the first time the plaintiff is seeking the claim in the year 2011 which is after a period of 12 years.
Therefore the plaintiff is not entitled to any relief since her claim is barred by time under law.
17. The EX.P2 is the sale deed executed by BDA in of defendant no.1.
As per EX P2 the defendant n.1 purchased the suit schedule property by paying the amount of Rs. 28, 614/- to BDA.
It is not the case of the plaintiff is that the defendant no. 1 had no other income to buy the schedule property.
It is also not the case of plaintiff is that defendant no. not given any share to her in compensation awarded for acquire of their land.
The plaintiff also not whispered about her fathers death whether he died prior to allotment of suit schedule property to defendant no.1.
It is admitted fact that the suit schedule property being a residential site was purchased by defendant no, 1 from BDA by paying amount of Rs.28,614/ sale consideration amount.

Merely because site was allotted under the incentive scheme to the defendant no.1 the mother of the plaintiff in lieu of land acquired by it , site does not become ancestral or joint family property nor it becomes the property acquired with the financial help of ancestral property.
18. Counsel for defendant No.2 contended that as per Section 14 of the Hindu Succession Act the suit property is the self acquired property of the defendant No.1.
Hence the plaintiff have no right to challenge the sale deed executed by the defendant No.1.
Admittedly the suit schedule property is allotted to defendant No.1 and hence it is the absolute property of defendant No.1 and the plaintiff cannot claim it as it is ancestral property.

Hence the suit of the plaintiff is barred under section 14 of Hindu Succession Act.
19.
As per section 14 of Hindu Succession Act property of female Hindu to be her absolute property.
Hence during her life time no one can entitle to share in her property.
She can dispose of it as per her own will and wish.
Additional issue no.1 was answered as negative, but at the time answering it as preliminary issue by observing that only trial of the suit can answer the said controversy.
Since the suit schedule property is self acquired property of the defendant no.1, the plaintiff does not have right challenge the sale deed executed by her mother defendant no.1 as null and void.

20. ISSUE No.3 :

The contention of the defendant No.2 is that the suit property is a site allotted to defendant No.1 and the same is the self acquired property and later the said property was sold to defendant No.2 by executing registered sale deed in the year 2002.
The contention of the plaintiff that defendant No.1 is her mother.

The suit schedule property was the ancestral property bearing Sy.No.191/1 of Agara village was owned by her grandmother late Smt.Motamma which was acquired by the BDA for formation of HSR Layout and in an oral partition the said property had fallen to the share of her father and subsequently said survey number was acquired by the BDA and the suit site was allotted to her mother under incentive scheme for the voluntarily surrender of Land Rules, 1989 and subsequently on 5/11/2001 the BDA has executed a registered sale deed of the suit property in favour of defendant No.1, but the plaintiff has not produced any document to show that the suit schedule property is the ancestral property of defendant No.1.This court also come to the conclusion that the suit schedule property is a self acquired property of defendant no.1.
Hence there is no cause of action to file the suit.
Accordingly, this court's answer to issue No.3 is answered in the negative.
21. ISSUE No.4 :

The defendant No.2 contended that the suit property was alienated by the defendant No.1 in the year 2002 in favour of defendant No.2 and the plaintiff filed a suit after lapse of 09 years.
22.
As per article 58 of limitation act the limitation period to obtain any other declaration is three years from the date of right to sue first accrues.
23. As per explanation No.I of section 3 of TP Act there is a constructive notice with respect compulsory registrable documents 24.
As per explanation No.II of section 3 of TP Act there is a constructive notice with respect possession.

Explanation 1 of Section 3 of T.P.Act reads as under:
Explanation 1-Where any transaction relating to immovable property is required by law to be and has been effected by a registered instrument, any person acquiring such property or any part of, or share or interest in, such property shall be deemed to have notice of such instrument as from the date of registration or, [where the property is not all situated in one sub-district, or where the registered instrument has been registered under sub-section (2) of section 30 of the Indian Registration Act, 1908 (16 of 1908), from the earliest date on which any memorandum of such registered instrument has been filed by any Sub-Registrar within whose sub-district any part13 pt of the property which is being acquired, or of the property wherein a share or interest is being acquired, is situated:]

Explanation 2 of Section 3 of T.P.Act reads as Prameela N vs Lakshmamma on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92622320/
8 under:
"Any person acquiring any immovable property or any share or interest in any such property shall be deemed to have notice of the title, if any, of any person who is for the time being in actual possession thereof".
25.
The plaintiff should have filed the suit at the prescribed time period i.e three years from the date of registration of sale deed.
There is an in ordinate delay of 9 years in filing the suit.
Hence, this court's answer to issue No.4 in the affirmative.

but as per Ex.D10 it discloses that the possession of the suit property was handed over to the defendant No.2 as on the date of execution of Ex.D.10.

27. ADDL. ISSUE No.2 :
The plaintiff herself admitted in her cross examination that there were 3 sites allotted to her mother i.e. defendant No.1.
In the suit she has claimed partition on only one site and other two sites are not included in this suit.
Hence the suit is bad for non inclusion of all the properties.

In this connection the defendant No.2 has relied upon a ruling reported in ILR 1998 KAR 681 (Sri Tukaram vs. Sambhaji and others) wherein it is held that the inclusion of all the joint family properties in the instant suit for partition was necessary and without bringing all the joint family properties into the hotchpot, the suit for partition of the shares of the members of the joint family is one property which amounts to partial partition is not maintainable.

28. ISSUE No.6:
The contention of the plaintiff is that the suit property is the ancestral property of plaintiff and defendant No.1 and she is entitle for half share in the suit schedule property.
In this connection she has not produced any document to show that the suit property is the ancestral property of plaintiff and defendant No.1 and she is entitle half share in the suit property.

She also admitted in her cross examination that she is residing in the property given by her mother .
29. The counsel for defendant no. 2 and 3 argued that the plaintiff and defendant no.1 are residing in the same address and they colluding with each other this suit has been filed by the plaintiff.
If she has share it can be adjusted in the site no.826.
Admittedly EX D4 discloses that the plaintiff and her husband and defendant no.1 are residing in the same address.
Suppose the suit schedule property is ancestral property and if she entitled to share, her share can be adjusted in site no. 826 which is retained by her mother defendant no.1.
Hence this court's answer to issue no. issue No.6 is in the negative.

opennyai_summary.facts:
After the death of plaintiff's father, the mother of the plaintiff i.e defendant No.1 was looking after the properties which fell to the share of late Nanjundappa.
Smt.Lakshmamma approached the BDA and sought for allotment under the scheme called Voluntary Surrender Scheme and the application of Smt.Lakshmamma was considered and allotment is made purely in favour of Smt.Lakshmamma and therefore the property becomes separate property of Smt.Lakshmamma.
The property acquired in the year 1987 and allotment was made in the year 2000 and therefore the amended provision of Section 6 of Hindu Succession Act is not applicable to the facts and circumstances of the case.
Therefore the plaintiff cannot claim any share in respect of the property which is allotted by the BDA in favour of Smt.Lakshmamma.
The allotment was made for a valuable consideration and a consideration of Rs.17,800/- was paid by Smt.Lakshmamma.
On payment of the said amount the said property was conveyed in favour of Smt.Lakshmamma and hence the said property is the absolute and separate property of Smt.Lakshmamma.
Plaintiff did not lay her claim for grant of compensation for receiving the compensation of Rs.3,40,847/-.
The plaintiff did not seek for any share in the property, the acquisition of which was complete during the year 1987.
For the first time the plaintiff is seeking the claim in the year 2011 which is after a period of 12 years.
Therefore the plaintiff is not entitled to any relief since her claim is barred by time under law.
The plaintiff made false averment that the property was allotted to the share of Nanjunda Reddy under family partition,
but the plaintiff failed to aver the date of such partition and failed to produce the partition deed to show that the said property was allotted to the share of Nanjunda Reddy.
After completion of acquisition proceedings a compensation of Rs.3,40,847/- was deposited in the civil court since all the legal heirs of Motamma had right over the said compensation.
Moreover there was no joint family concept existing in view of the absence of even a single male member of the family.
opennyai_summary.issue:

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
On account of the said fact the plaintiff has caused legal injury to the extent of her half share in the suit schedule property and the said alienation is not binding on the plaintiff and now the defendant No.2 is trying to alienate the schedule property with the sole intention to deprive the plaintiff's right.
Defendant No.1 approached the BDA and sought for allotment under the scheme called Voluntary Surrender Scheme and the application of defendant No.1 was considered and allotment is made purely in favour of defendant No.1 and therefore the property becomes separate property of defendant No.1.
The property acquired in the year 1987 and allotment was made in the year 2000 and therefore the amended provision of Section 6 of Hindu Succession Act is not applicable to the facts and circumstances of the case.
Therefore the plaintiff cannot claim any share in respect of the property which is allotted by the BDA in favour of defendant No.1.
The allotment was made for a valuable consideration and a consideration of Rs.17,800/- was paid by defendant No.1.
On payment of the said amount the said property was conveyed in favour of defendant No.1 and hence the said property is the absolute and separate property of defendant No.1.
Therefore the claim of plaintiff with respect to schedule property is frivolous and mischievous.
The plaintiff did not seek for any share in the property, the acquisition of which was complete during the year 1987.
For the first time the plaintiff is seeking the claim in the year 2011 which is after a period of 12 years.
Therefore the plaintiff is not entitled to any relief since her claim is barred by time under law.
Merely because site was allotted under the incentive scheme to the defendant no.1 the mother of the plaintiff in lieu of land acquired by it , site does not become ancestral or joint family property nor it becomes the property acquired with the financial help of ancestral property.
Hence the suit of the plaintiff is barred under section 14 of Hindu Succession Act.
19.
As per section 14 of Hindu Succession Act property of female Hindu to be her absolute property.
Hence during her life time no one can entitle to share in her property.
The defendant No.2 contended that the suit property was alienated by the defendant No.1 in the year 2002 in favour of defendant No.2 and the plaintiff filed a suit after lapse of 09 years.
22.
opennyai_summary.arguments: In this connection the defendant No.2 has relied upon a ruling reported in ILR 1998 KAR 681 (Sri Tukaram vs. Sambhaji and others) wherein it is held that the inclusion of all the joint family properties in the instant suit for partition was necessary and without bringing all the joint family properties into the hotchpot, the suit for partition of the shares of the members of the joint family is one property which amounts to partial partition is not maintainable.
opennyai_summary.decision: Hence this court's answer to issue no. issue No.7 is in the negative.
